answers.answer: An Exile who takes the title during their Act normally first flips it to Usurper at their next Wake, after the Wake victory check; if still Usurper, they can first win at the following Wake. If the title is lost and later retaken, it resets to Oathkeeper, restarting that sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Usurper victory: ‘surviving to next Wake to flip, then surviving to following Wake to win’; ‘Losing and retaking title resets it to Oathkeeper.’ Wake order says victory is checked before the title flip.

answers.answer: Supremacy—Conquest; People—Rebellion; Protection—Sanctuary; Devotion—Faith. A Visionary win also requires an Exile to have the true Vision revealed, complete its goal at Wake, and have at least 3 Visions drawn from the world deck. A ‘most’ goal for Conquest or Sanctuary requires strictly more than every other player; ties do not count.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions table and Visionary victory paragraph: ‘at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck’; ‘strictly more than every other player, no ties.’

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, and 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Stable regime: rolls at ends of rounds 5–7 only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper; results are ‘6 / 5–6 / 3–6’; an Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

answers.answer: Round 8 ends automatically. Priority is: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, the Empire wins, with a qualifying Citizen Successor winning alone instead of the Chancellor; (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions ordered Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise the Empire wins, again with a qualifying Successor replacing the Chancellor. The final Empire fallback applies even if an Exile is Oathkeeper only.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → War exhaustion, ordered checks 1–4.

answers.answer: Supremacy: hold more relics and banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a true Vision or by becoming Usurper; those victory paths are for Exiles.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table gives the four Successor goals; Visionary victory states ‘Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.’

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, either add 1 favor from your board to it or return 1 favor from it to a least-full suit bank, choosing among tied banks. Never remove its last favor: at 1, add if able; if you have none, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After the choice or choices, check whether it has 6 or more favor and flip it to Mob. Reaching the threshold in that final check does not cause another payment that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake → mandatory order, item 1: describes the two choices, last-favor rule, Mob-side repeat, then 6+ threshold flip and no retroactive repeat.

answers.answer: Rest order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; save remaining Supply; then optionally use Rest powers once each in chosen order. Exiles and Chancellor refresh to the space determined by their warbands remaining in personal bank. A Citizen refreshes to exactly the Chancellor's marker space, including the leftmost space, without counting purple warbands. To save unspent Supply, move the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost (7 Supply).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Rest: numbered mandatory order, refresh instructions, and ‘Save remaining unspent Supply’ rule.

answers.answer: Search may use either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces that cost with 2, while other applicable modifiers still apply. Draw 3 unless the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it; you cannot voluntarily stop early. From the world deck draw one at a time, and on drawing a Vision announce it, stop immediately, and advance Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile neither stops the draw nor advances the track. If the source empties, take only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search: source/cost paragraph and draw/stop rules distinguish world-deck Visions from discard-pile Visions.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; order multiple discards as you choose. For cards from hand/advisers, use the pawn's region. For a card discarded from a site in another region, use that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching bank; secrets go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search → Discard destinations gives the regional cycle, hand/adviser and remote-site rules, and resource destinations.

answers.answer: There are at most 3 advisers total, counting faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser subject to locked-card rules. If an incoming card changes the adviser limit, check against the new limit before playing it; for multiple limits use the lowest. A facedown adviser has no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card (including a site-only card or Vision) may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser can be played faceup as a minor action as if finishing Search, following destination and card-play restrictions/effects; it is not an unrestricted in-place flip. An Exile may play a true Vision faceup into the separate Revealed Vision space, replacing and discarding the old revealed Vision; it uses no adviser slot. Chancellor and Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Actions → Search → Adviser and True Vision; Minor actions says to play a facedown adviser faceup as if finishing Search; it is ‘not simply an unrestricted in-place flip.’

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: at the pawn's site, put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets already) and gain 2 warbands from personal bank to board; Citizens gain purple. Relics and ruins are ineligible, and you need not rule the site. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen or intact edifice at the pawn's site. Option one: put 1 secret on it and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank. Option two: put 2 favor on it and gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers do not match; if none match, the second option gains zero secrets. Costs remain payable even when a gain is zero, and finite favor/warband sources provide only what is available; secrets are unlimited.
answers.evidence: Actions → Muster and Trade give costs, eligible cards, placement and gains; Trade states ‘With no matching advisers gain zero secrets’ and source limits.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus any site relic cost when recovering a facedown relic at your site; pay the printed cost and hold the relic faceup in your personal bank. Either banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by paying strictly more of its resource than it currently has. For People's Favor, put the paid favor on it, distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks starting at a chosen bank and moving through the printed bank order, and flip it to normal side if Mob; the previous holder gets none of the old favor. For Darkest Secret, put paid secrets on it; the new holder takes one old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. Recovery from yourself returns all old secrets to yourself; from the shared bank, the remainder stays there. Banner recovery has no seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Actions → Recover: target/cost rules and separate People's Favor and Darkest Secret resolution bullets.

answers.answer: To recover another player's Darkest Secret, their pawn's site must contain a suited card matching none of their faceup advisers; if that condition is met it is recoverable. With no faceup advisers, a suited site card still matches none and the banner is recoverable. An empty site or ruin-only site protects it because neither provides a suited card. Ruins and facedown advisers have no suit. Recovery from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection.
answers.evidence: Actions → Recover → Darkest Secret protection: requires a suited card at the holder's pawn site matching none of their faceup advisers; explicitly covers no advisers, empty sites, and ruin-only sites.

answers.answer: A legal defender is any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, bandits may be chosen. At least one target must be at the attacker's pawn site; if the defender rules that site, it must be targeted. The attacker may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, one defense die per site. If the defender's pawn is at the attacker's site, the attacker may additionally target their relics (printed defense dice), banners (one die per resource on the banner), or pawn and favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target itself satisfies the local-target requirement.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign, steps 1–2, defines defender eligibility and local, remote, relic, banner, and pawn/favor targets.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Defense is shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol with multipliers stacking, plus defending warbands at targeted sites and the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any target; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Doubles multiply shields only. Each attack skull immediately kills one of the attacker's force warbands. Count full swords, and each pair of hollow swords adds 1 attack; a lone hollow sword adds zero. The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, with no excess sacrifice. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower score means defender wins.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign, steps 2, 4, and 5: dice pools, shield multipliers, warband defense, skulls, hollow swords, sacrifice, and strict-win rule.

answers.answer: First resolve defeat: the defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. If the attacker wins, they may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; zero leaves a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. A banner seized by any method except Recover loses 2 resources, down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Shrouded Wood overrides the attacker's destination choice if its enemy ruler chooses the destination. Battle-plan effects resolve at their specified times, and Supremacy title transfer occurs at the end of Campaign.
answers.evidence: Actions → Campaign, steps 6–8, covers defeat, winning placements/targets, banner seizure, banishment via pawn-and-favor, Shrouded Wood, and effects/timing.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a targeted site. Defender and Allies activate their ruled Campaign modifiers; the title defense bonus is shared, and allied board warbands count only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; each pays, and a plan cannot be used by multiple players. The Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; site survivors return to the Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizen board warbands stay on those boards. Side-wide power references apply to the whole side, but ‘your site/board’ remain individual. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make every Citizen non-Imperial: only specified attackers/defenders lose Imperial status. Specifically, a Citizen attacking Chancellor or another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; if Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
answers.evidence: Campaign step 1 and Imperial defense bullets state the non-Imperial cases, Chancellor ally, other allies, modifier/plan use, force deaths, and side interpretation.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs (from rows to destination columns): from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, 2, 2, 2; from Hinterland, 4, 2, 3. Travel goes to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. On revealing a facedown destination, put its printed favor/secrets there from the shared bank and its printed number of relics beside it facedown from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number Travel costs first, then other increases/decreases. A modifier that says to spend no Supply overrides all cost increases. Entry restrictions still apply unless specifically ignored.
answers.evidence: Actions → Travel gives the cost matrix, reveal/stocking procedure, and order of fixed costs and modifiers; says no-Supply overrides increases.

answers.answer: During play, the Grand Scepter holder (even an Exile) may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, or exile another Citizen. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; it may additionally negotiate binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may let the recipient peek at Reliquary relics. The offer is accepted by flipping to Citizen and replacing that player's board/map warbands with purple (if purple is short, the new Citizen chooses what to remove and replace). They discard a revealed Vision, flip their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end their Act if accepting during their turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Promised pieces are exchanged and the Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers apply acceptance without a negotiated offer. The summary also says a Citizen who self-exiles without holding the Scepter pays its holder favor equal to own board warbands plus all their secrets on board and on denizen/relic/edifice cards, then flips to Exile, replaces board purple with own color, refreshes fully, and ends Act.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play → Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, and Self-exile paragraphs.

answers.answer: A Vision-only victory makes the next Oath match that Vision. Any other victory method, or multiple methods, lets the winner choose any Oath except the current one; save the goal in the World Box. If an Exile wins, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed boards, to Exile. The winner may offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; each accepting player flips their board to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband at that site. Rebuild the world deck by shuffling all denizens remaining in play (excluding those at sites, in Archive, or Dispossessed), then make a top stack of 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions (12 cards total), middle stack of 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions (18 cards), with remaining denizens below. The Chronicle aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ is identified as incorrect; the summary specifies 10 plus 2, so the top stack is not 14 cards.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle steps 1–2 and 9: Oath choice, Citizenship turnover, and deck stacks; step 9 explicitly corrects the aid's 14-card top stack.
